trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Going up would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going down would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right, the next 10 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4). So the line goes up.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5); going to number 5, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (up from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go right.
I can't rule out up or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
I can't rule out left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going up, the next 10 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes left.
Going down would force the line onto number 8 before its turn; going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes left.
Going right, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 6; going to number 5, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from number 2) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
The line must go left: up is number 11, which comes later.
Going up, the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes left.
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (3,5).

Going around the edge to (5,5) would force the line onto number 8 before its turn; going around the edge to (1,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2). So the line goes left.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would leave both number 9 and number 8 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Number 8 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (1,2) would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (1,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 10 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 22/25 cells (88%).
Generation 1: fitness 15/25. The best line covers 23 cells, the first 15 of them still look solvable.
Generation 2: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 2: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 48 futures: 100% survive going right (best covers 60%); up 83%.
Tried 48 futures: 88% survive going up (best covers 60%); down 79%.
Jackpot! A future after going right covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 1,428 variables and 3,885 clauses in 0.00 s (413 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
